food.name: Feta

identity.basisReason: Per-100g as-sold cheese basis matches the USDA record and FoodRanked's packaged-food convention.

scoreReadiness.summary: Canonical feta entry with exact USDA nutrient and amino-acid rows, including a source-derived 9-of-9 essential amino-acid result.
caveats: Feta recipes and brines vary; this entry represents the generic USDA cheese identity rather than every branded feta.

sourceNotes: Production source pass for plain feta cheese.
All displayed nutrition values use a per-100g basis.
Primary nutrient and amino-acid identity is USDA FoodData Central FDC 173420.
The Protected Designation of Origin context comes from the European Commission's feta registration page.

topPros.title: a little feta can change a whole plate
topPros.explanation: The salty tang means a small crumble can wake up salads, eggs, wraps, and vegetables.

topPros.title: real feta has a Protected Designation of Origin
topPros.explanation: In the European Union, it has to come from Greece and use sheep's milk, sometimes mixed with goat's milk.

topPros.title: the crumble format is genuinely useful
topPros.explanation: You can spread flavour across a meal without needing a thick slab of cheese.

topCons.title: the salt is the real catch
topCons.explanation: Brining pushes sodium to roughly 1.1 grams per 100 grams, so portions matter even before the saturated fat gets involved.

topCons.title: it is still a dairy food
topCons.explanation: Milk allergy or poor dairy tolerance can rule it out completely.

topCons.title: the sharp flavour can take over
topCons.explanation: Feta works brilliantly as an accent, but it is not always what you want dominating the entire meal.

explanation.summary: Proteins are carrying this food most, while fats are holding it back most. It lands in A tier.
explanation.whyThisTier: This food lands in A tier with a display score of 80. Section scores: fats 21.5, carbs 70, proteins 86.7, vitamins 50, minerals 22, pros 50, cons 50.

closing.summary: Best bits are complete protein, huge vitamin B12, strong calcium and zinc, and loads of flavour from a small amount. Weak spots are saturated fat, very high sodium, almost no potassium, and the fact that normal portions are much smaller than 100 grams. Best used as a flavour booster rather than the main event. Crumble a little over vegetables, grains, or eggs and let the rest of the meal provide the volume.

scenes.narrationText: 21.5 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 13.3 grams, which is a seriously heavy mark even for cheese. Cholesterol is 89 milligrams, adding another downside, while polyunsaturated fat is only 0.59 grams and cannot do much to balance things out. For dairy, fat can bring richness, but this particular fat mix comes with plenty of baggage.

For dairy, useful protein matters, and feta brings a respectable amount even though it is normally eaten in fairly small servings.

scenes.narrationText: Vitamin B12 is 70% daily value, which is the surprise star here. B12 supports the nerves and helps make red blood cells that carry oxygen around the body. Vitamin A is 14% daily value, adding some vision and immune support, but vitamin D is only 2%. For dairy, the B12 result is excellent even though the rest of the vitamin panel is much less exciting.

scenes.narrationText: Calcium is 38% daily value, a strong amount for bones, teeth, and normal muscle function. Zinc is 26% daily value, giving useful support for immunity and wound healing. Potassium is only 1% daily value though, so feta brings almost nothing for fluid balance. For dairy, calcium is the headline mineral, with zinc as a genuinely useful bonus.

scenes.narrationText: The upsides first: a little feta can change a whole plate. The salty tang means a small crumble can wake up salads, eggs, wraps, and vegetables. Real Protected Designation of Origin feta has a protected origin story. In the European Union, it has to come from Greece and use sheep's milk, sometimes mixed with goat's milk. The crumble format is genuinely useful. You can spread flavour across a meal without needing a thick slab of cheese.
